To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) privacy is a complex and multi-faceted concept, (b) GDPR is a complex, multi-faceted and multi-level regulation, and (c) UML use case diagram is a powerful and flexible tool to depict privacy and GDPR requirements.
(1) GDPR is an EU regulation, which will come into force on 25 May 2018 and will apply directly in all EU Member States.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) How can the UML notation help in GDPR privacy compliance?
the following questions: (1) How to design a GDPR compliant educational e-platform?
the following: 1) How to model privacy in UML use case diagram.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EU GDPR has a strong impact on the e-learning industry and its stakeholders, as it affects both the data processing activities and the data subjects.
the GDPR is a complex and demanding set of rules and regulations, and it is not easy to comply with it.
the GDPR is a very complex piece of legislation, which has to be taken into account by any company that collects, uses, stores or transmits personal data of individuals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we managed to map GDPR’s requirements in UML use case models.
the proposed methodology is a first step towards the development of an automated tool for the analysis of GDPR privacy requirements in UML.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GDPR can be incorporated into a software design by using UML use case diagramming.
the UML diagrams can be used as a means of communication among software engineers, legal experts, and business analysts.
privacy is a design concern and should be addressed from the very start of the design process.
